deals.headline: Rob Walton bought 10% of the Diamondbacks at a $2bn valuation
deals.summary: Broncos owner Rob Walton bought a 10% stake in 2024 at a $2 billion valuation; the transaction was never announced. Sportico reports the team used the bulk of the proceeds for Chase Field improvements.

deals.evidence: The diversions of these taxes over the next 30 years will raise up to $500 million for renovations to Chase Field.
deals.headline: Arizona diverts stadium taxes for up to $500m of Chase Field renovations
deals.summary: Gov. Katie Hobbs signed HB 2704, diverting taxes generated at Chase Field and district buildings to a renovation fund for 30 years, raising up to $500 million (inflation-adjusted); the Diamondbacks contribute $250 million of their own.

name: Arizona Diamondbacks
notes: US teams publish no accounts: revenue (net of revenue sharing and stadium debt service), operating income (EBITDA) and player expenses are Forbes estimates for the 2025 season, published March 2026; Forbes ranks the team #19. Forbes lists Chase Field at 48,618 seats; MLB.com gives 48,633 (used). Founded: 1995 is when the expansion franchise was awarded; first season 1998. Kendrick's own percentage is not published. The Walton deal is press-reported (anonymous sources), not club-confirmed. Domain is the club section of mlb.com (dbacks.com redirects there). No legal entity, attendance, socials or honours sourced on a citable page.

ownership_summary: Controlled by managing general partner Ken Kendrick, who was part of the 1995 expansion group and bought control in 2004 at a $238 million valuation. Broncos owner Rob Walton bought a 10% minority stake in 2024 at a $2 billion valuation (reported by Sportico in March 2026; never announced by the club). No institutional fund holder is on record.
